decks.title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Frog — Part 1: Morphology, digestion, respiration and circulation
goals: Describe the external features of a frog and distinguish a male from a female
Trace the path of food through the alimentary canal and explain how a frog respires through skin, buccal cavity and lungs
Describe the heart and the route of blood in the frog

slides.heading: The frog
slides.body_md: Part 1 — the body of the common frog and its digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems.

visual.alt: Morphology, digestion, respiration and circulation as the topics of part one

slides.narration: The frog is an amphibian that lives both in water and on land. In this part we look at its outer form, how it digests food, how it breathes through skin, mouth and lungs, and how its three-chambered heart sends blood round the body.

slides.heading: External features of the frog
slides.body_md: The body has a **head** and a **trunk**; there is **no neck and no tail**. The moist skin is olive green above with dark spots, and pale yellow below.

slides.narration: Two bulging eyes and two nostrils lie on the top of the head, and a round tympanum behind each eye receives sound. The short forelimbs have four digits. The long hind limbs have five toes joined by webs, which make them powerful paddles.

slides.heading: Features and their uses
slides.body_md: Every external feature has a use on land or in water.

rows: Gas exchange, absorbing water; spots give camouflage
Bulging eyes with a nictitating membrane
Wide view; the membrane protects the eye under water
Support the body when it lands
Exit for faeces, urine and gametes

visual.alt: Table of external features of the frog and their uses

slides.narration: The skin must stay moist because the frog breathes through it. A clear nictitating membrane covers each eye under water. The hind legs are long and webbed for leaping and swimming. The cloacal opening at the rear lets out faeces, urine and gametes.

slides.heading: Male and female frogs
slides.body_md: A **male** has **vocal sacs** that swell when he calls and a **copulatory pad** on the first digit of each forelimb. A **female** has neither.

slides.narration: Males call to attract females, and the vocal sacs act as resonators that make the sound louder. The rough dark copulatory pad on the first finger helps the male to grip the female during mating. Females have smooth forelimbs and no vocal sacs.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: a pond census
slides.body_md: A pond has 120 frogs, males to females in the ratio 3 to 2. Each male has two vocal sacs. Find the numbers of males and females and of vocal sacs.
bullets: Parts = 3 + 2 = 5; one part = 120 ÷ 5 = 24.
Vocal sacs = 72 × 2 = **144**; the females have none.

visual.alt: Worked table: 72 males, 48 females, 144 vocal sacs

slides.narration: Share the total in the given ratio. Add the parts, find the value of one part, then multiply. Only the males have vocal sacs, two each, so multiply the number of males by two.

slides.body_md: The canal is **short**, as the frog is a **carnivore**: mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, **stomach**, **duodenum**, **ileum**, **rectum** and **cloaca**.

slides.narration: The frog catches insects with its sticky bilobed tongue, which is fixed at the front of the mouth and flicked out. Food passes through the buccal cavity, pharynx and oesophagus to the stomach, then the small intestine, the rectum and the cloaca.

slides.heading: Digestion and the digestive glands
slides.body_md: The liver, gall bladder and pancreas discharge into the duodenum.

rows: Hydrochloric acid and gastric juice begin digestion; food becomes chyme
Makes pancreatic juice with digestive enzymes
Receives bile and pancreatic juice through a common duct
Final digestion; absorption by villi and microvilli

visual.alt: Table of parts of the alimentary canal and their roles

slides.narration: Chyme leaves the stomach for the duodenum, where bile from the liver and pancreatic juice join it through one common duct. Digestion is completed in the intestine, and the digested food is absorbed through finger-like villi. Waste goes to the rectum and the cloaca.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: feeding and gut length
slides.body_md: (a) A frog eats 6 insects a day. How many insects does it eat in 30 days? (b) A frog 7 cm long has an intestine 8.4 cm long; a tadpole 3 cm long has an intestine 30 cm long. Compare the gut with the body length in each.

slides.heading: Worked example 3: pumping and oxygen
slides.body_md: (a) The heart beats 45 times a minute and the ventricle pumps 0.06 ml each beat. How much blood does it pump in a minute and in an hour? (b) A frog on land takes up 2 ml of oxygen an hour: 45 percent through the skin, 50 percent through the lungs and the rest through the buccal cavity. Find each amount.
bullets: (b) Skin: 2 × 45 ÷ 100 = **0.9 ml**; lungs: **1 ml**; buccal cavity: **0.1 ml**.

visual.alt: Worked table of blood pumped and oxygen taken up

slides.narration: Multiply the number of beats by the volume of each beat to get the output in a minute, then by sixty for an hour. For the oxygen, take the given share of the total for each surface. The skin and the lungs together supply nearly all of it.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Body: head and trunk, no neck or tail; moist skin; bulging eyes, tympanum; webbed hind limbs. Male: vocal sacs and copulatory pad.
Alimentary canal: mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, ileum, rectum, cloaca; short because the frog is a carnivore. Liver, gall bladder and pancreas open into the duodenum.
Respiration: skin in water; skin, buccal cavity and lungs on land.
Heart: two atria and one ventricle; closed circulation; portal systems.

rows: Short canal; bile and pancreatic juice into duodenum
Three-chambered heart, mixed blood in ventricle

visual.alt: Summary table of digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems

slides.narration: To recap: the frog has a smooth moist skin and webbed hind limbs; a short digestive tract with liver and pancreas pouring into the duodenum; three ways of breathing; and a three-chambered heart in which the blood mixes in the ventricle.

slides.heading: Exam tips
bullets: Write the **order** of the alimentary canal without missing a part.
Name **where bile and pancreatic juice enter**: the duodenum.
Say that the heart has **two atria and one ventricle** and that blood **mixes** in the ventricle.
Give the **three surfaces** for respiration and say which is used in water.
slides.narration: Exam tips. Write the parts of the canal in order. Say that bile and pancreatic juice enter the duodenum. Remember two atria and one ventricle, with mixing. And name the skin, mouth lining and lungs as the three surfaces for breathing.

slides.heading: Urine and gametes reach the cloaca
slides.body_md: The **cloaca** is a common chamber for faeces, urine and gametes. The two sexes differ in the ducts that open into it.

rows: Pair of testes, attached to the kidneys
Pair of ovaries, no functional link with the kidneys

visual.alt: Table comparing the ducts of the male and the female frog

slides.narration: In the male, one duct carries both urine and sperms. In the female, the ureters carry urine and the oviducts carry ova, and they open separately into the cloaca. The urinary bladder lies in front of the rectum and opens into the cloaca in both sexes.

slides.heading: Fertilisation and development
slides.body_md: Fertilisation is **external** and takes place in **water**; development is **indirect**, through a **tadpole**.

rows: Male clasps the female; she lays ova, he sheds sperms
Develops into a tadpole, which breathes by gills
Tadpole changes into a young frog with lungs and limbs

visual.alt: Table of fertilisation and development in the frog

slides.narration: The female lays her ova in water and the male sheds sperms over them, so fertilisation is external. A large number of ova are laid because many are lost. The tadpole that hatches changes by metamorphosis into an adult frog.

slides.narration: The brain lies inside the cranium. The forebrain has the olfactory lobes for smell, the cerebral hemispheres and the diencephalon. The midbrain has two optic lobes. The hindbrain has the cerebellum, which balances, and the medulla oblongata, which continues as the spinal cord.

slides.heading: Nervous system and sense organs
slides.body_md: The nervous system has central, peripheral and autonomic parts.

rows: Ten pairs of cranial nerves from the brain and spinal nerves
Touch, taste, smell, sight and hearing; the ear has a tympanum and an inner ear

visual.alt: Table of the nervous system and sense organs of the frog

slides.narration: The brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system. Ten pairs of cranial nerves arise from the brain. The sense organs include organs of touch, taste, smell, sight and hearing, and the ear consists of the tympanum and an internal ear.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: nerve conduction
slides.body_md: A nerve 0.15 m long carries an impulse at 30 m per second. How many milliseconds does the impulse take to travel along it?
bullets: Time = distance ÷ speed = 0.15 ÷ 30 = 0.005 second.
1 second = 1000 milliseconds, so the time is **5 milliseconds**.

visual.alt: Worked table: 5 milliseconds

slides.narration: Divide the distance by the speed to get the time in seconds, then multiply by one thousand to change to milliseconds. The impulse crosses this short nerve in five thousandths of a second.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Kidneys remove urea (ureotelic); male ureter is a urinogenital duct; female ureter and oviduct open separately into the cloaca.
Brain: forebrain (olfactory lobes, hemispheres, diencephalon), midbrain (optic lobes), hindbrain (cerebellum, medulla oblongata); ten pairs of cranial nerves.
Reproduction: testes and ovaries; external fertilisation in water; tadpole and metamorphosis.

slides.narration: To recap: the frog excretes urea through its kidneys, its brain is divided into forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain, and it reproduces by external fertilisation in water, with a tadpole that undergoes metamorphosis.

notes.title: Structural Organisation in Animals: Frog — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Morphology of the frog
sections.body_md:
The common Indian frog (*Rana tigrina*) lives in water and on land; it is an **amphibian**. Its body is divided into **head** and **trunk**; there is **no neck and no tail** in the adult.

**Skin.** The skin is **smooth, slimy and always moist** because of mucus. The **dorsal** surface is olive green with irregular dark spots, which gives **camouflage**; the **ventral** surface is pale yellow. The frog does not drink water but absorbs it through the skin, and it can change colour slightly to hide from enemies.

**Head.** A pair of **bulging eyes** with a transparent **nictitating membrane** that protects them in water; a pair of **nostrils** at the tip of the snout; and a **tympanum** (the ear drum) on each side behind the eye, which receives sound.

**Limbs.** The **forelimbs** are short, with **four digits**, and support the body. The **hind limbs** are long and muscular with **five webbed toes**, used for **leaping, swimming and burrowing**. A **cloacal aperture** at the posterior end lets out faeces, urine and gametes.

**Sexes.** A **male** has a pair of **vocal sacs** (resonators for the call) and a rough **copulatory pad** on the first digit of each forelimb, which helps to grip the female. A **female** has neither.

key_terms.definition_md: The ear drum on each side of the head of a frog.
A transparent membrane that protects the eye under water.
A throat pouch of the male that amplifies his call.
A rough pad on the first digit of the male forelimb.

sections.heading: 2. Digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems (brief account)
sections.body_md:
**Digestive system.** The **alimentary canal is short**, because the frog is a **carnivore** (it eats insects, worms and small animals). Order: **mouth → buccal cavity → pharynx → oesophagus → stomach → duodenum → ileum → rectum → cloaca**. Food is caught by the **bilobed tongue**, which is attached at the front of the mouth. **Digestion:** in the stomach, **hydrochloric acid and gastric juice** digest food, which becomes **chyme** and passes to the **duodenum**. The **liver** makes **bile**, stored in the **gall bladder**; the **pancreas** makes **pancreatic juice** with enzymes; both are poured into the duodenum through a **common duct**. Digestion is completed in the intestine, and absorption takes place through **villi and microvilli**. Undigested waste passes to the rectum and out of the **cloaca**.

**Respiratory system.** *In water:* **cutaneous respiration** — dissolved oxygen diffuses across the moist skin. *On land:* the **skin**, the **buccal cavity** and the **lungs**. The **lungs** are a pair of elongated, pink, sac-like organs in the thorax. **Pulmonary respiration:** air enters through the nostrils into the buccal cavity; when the floor of the buccal cavity is raised, air is forced through the glottis into the lungs. During hibernation and aestivation the frog breathes through the skin alone.

**Circulatory system.** The circulation is **closed**: blood in vessels, with **lymph** as well. The **heart** is **three-chambered** — **right and left atria and one ventricle** — enclosed in a **pericardium**. The **sinus venosus** joins the right atrium, and the **truncus arteriosus** arises from the ventricle. Blood from the body enters the right atrium, and blood from the lungs enters the left atrium (blood from the skin returns through the cutaneous veins with the body blood); **both open into the ventricle, where the blood is mixed**. There are two **portal systems**: the **hepatic portal system** (intestine to liver) and the **renal portal system** (hind limbs to kidneys). The red blood cells are **nucleated** and oval.

*Where books differ.* Some books give the exact pumping of the buccal floor in more detail, or list the arches leaving the truncus arteriosus; the notes follow the brief account in the syllabus.

sections.heading: 3. Excretory, nervous and reproductive systems (brief account)
sections.body_md:
**Excretory system.** A pair of compact, dark red, bean-shaped **kidneys** lies on each side of the backbone. Each is made of many **nephrons** (uriniferous tubules). The frog is **ureotelic**: it excretes **urea**. In the **male** the **ureters** act as **urinogenital ducts**, carrying urine and sperms to the **cloaca**; in the **female** the **ureters** and **oviducts** open **separately** into the cloaca. A thin-walled **urinary bladder** in front of the rectum opens into the cloaca.

**Nervous system.** **Central:** the **brain** (in the cranium) and the **spinal cord**; **peripheral:** **ten pairs of cranial nerves** and the spinal nerves; and an **autonomic** system. The brain has a **forebrain** (two **olfactory lobes**, two **cerebral hemispheres**, the **diencephalon**), a **midbrain** (two **optic lobes**) and a **hindbrain** (the **cerebellum** and the **medulla oblongata**, which passes out through the foramen magnum and continues as the spinal cord). **Sense organs** are for touch, taste, smell, sight and hearing; the ear has a **tympanum** and an inner ear only.

**Reproductive system.** *Male:* a pair of yellowish **testes** attached to the kidneys; fine **vasa efferentia** carry sperms into the kidney, and the **urinogenital duct** takes them to the cloaca. *Female:* a pair of **ovaries** near the kidneys, with no functional connection with them; **oviducts** open separately into the cloaca. **Fertilisation is external**, in water; **development is indirect** through a **tadpole**, which undergoes **metamorphosis**. A female lays a large number of ova at a time, since many are lost.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Giving the frog a neck or a tail.
- Saying that the alimentary canal is long; it is short because the frog is a carnivore.
- Saying that the stomach receives bile; bile and pancreatic juice enter the **duodenum**.
- Writing that the frog heart has four chambers, or that the blood in the ventricle is unmixed.
- Saying that a frog breathes only through lungs, or only through skin.
- Writing that in a female frog the oviducts and ureters join; they open separately into the cloaca.
- Writing that fertilisation in a frog is internal.

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1-mark subparts: a part of the canal, the number of chambers of the heart, a lettered figure, a give-a-reason.
- 2- and 3-mark questions: male against female; the organs of respiration; the path of food; the ducts of the male and the female.
- 5-mark questions in parts: a labelled diagram of the alimentary canal, urinogenital system or brain with a short account.

options.text_md: a female, because of the copulatory pads
a male, because of the copulatory pads and vocal sacs
a female, because of the vocal sacs
a male, because it has webbed toes

questions.solution_md: Copulatory pads and vocal sacs are features of the male — option (b).

questions.solution_md: B is the tympanum, the ear drum — option (b).

questions.stem_md: A frog sits motionless among wet leaves and is hard to see. Its upper surface is olive green with irregular dark spots. This colouring helps the frog by

options.text_md: camouflage, which hides it from enemies

questions.solution_md: The colour pattern blends with the background and hides the frog — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A frog swims with its eyes open under water. A clear structure that slides over each eye to protect it is the
questions.solution_md: The nictitating membrane protects the eye under water — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The skin of a frog must be kept moist.

**Reason (R):** Oxygen dissolves in the film of mucus on the skin and diffuses across it into the blood.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is true and Reason is false.
Both Assertion and Reason are false.

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and R explains A: gas exchange across the skin needs a moist surface — option (a).

questions.stem_md: True or false? The body of an adult frog has a distinct head, neck and trunk.
questions.solution_md: False: the head joins the trunk directly; there is no neck.

questions.stem_md: The round membrane behind each eye of a frog, which receives sound, is the ______.
questions.solution_md: Tympanum.

questions.stem_md: Give a reason: the hind limbs of a frog are longer and more muscular than the forelimbs.

answer.model_answer_md: They push the body forward in leaping and in swimming, so they must be long and strong.

questions.solution_md: Leaping and swimming.

questions.stem_md: Give a reason: only male frogs have vocal sacs.

answer.model_answer_md: Males call to attract females, and the sacs amplify the call.

questions.solution_md: Calling.

questions.stem_md: Frog X calls loudly at night and has a rough dark swelling on the first digit of each forelimb; frog Y has neither. Name the sex of X and the two structures, and state the use of each.

answer.model_answer_md: **X is a male.** The throat sacs are **vocal sacs**, which act as resonators and make the call louder to attract females. The rough swelling on the first digit is the **copulatory pad**, which helps the male to **grip the female** when he clasps her in mating.

questions.solution_md: Sex; two structures with uses.

questions.stem_md: State two features of the skin of a frog and give the use of each.

answer.model_answer_md: The skin is **moist and slimy** because of mucus, which keeps it wet so that dissolved gases can pass through it in **cutaneous respiration**. Its **olive green colour with dark spots** gives **camouflage**, helping the frog to hide from enemies among leaves and mud.

questions.solution_md: Two features with uses.

questions.stem_md: Describe the external features of a frog under the heads: divisions of the body, eyes and ears, and limbs.

answer.model_answer_md: The body has a **head and a trunk**, with **no neck and no tail**. The head bears a pair of **bulging eyes** with a **nictitating membrane**, a pair of **nostrils**, and a **tympanum** on each side behind the eye as the ear. The **forelimbs** are short with **four digits**; the **hind limbs** are long and muscular with **five webbed toes**.

questions.solution_md: Body, eyes and ears, limbs.

marking_scheme.step: Head and trunk; no neck or tail

questions.stem_md: A frog leaps across a lawn, swims in a pond and burrows into mud in the dry season. Explain how its limbs, eyes and skin suit this life in water and on land.

answer.model_answer_md: The **long, muscular hind limbs** push it in leaps, and their **webbed toes** act as paddles when it swims; the short forelimbs absorb the shock of landing. The **bulging eyes** let it see all round while its body is hidden, and the **nictitating membrane** protects them under water. The **moist skin** exchanges gases in water and in mud, and its colour gives camouflage.

questions.solution_md: Limbs, eyes, skin.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of a frog seen from above, naming at least six parts. [3]
(b) State two features that help a frog to live on land and in water. [2]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A frog with a **head** and **trunk**; two **eyes**, two **nostrils**, a **tympanum** on each side; short **forelimbs** with four digits; long **hind limbs** with five **webbed toes**; labelled.

(b) The **moist skin** allows breathing through the skin in water, and the **webbed hind limbs** allow swimming in water and leaping on land. The **lungs** and buccal cavity allow breathing in air.

questions.solution_md: Labelled frog; two features.

questions.stem_md: A pond has 150 frogs, males to females in the ratio 2 to 3. Every male has two vocal sacs. How many vocal sacs are there in the pond?
questions.solution_md: Males $= 150 \div 5 \times 2 = 60$; vocal sacs $= 60 \times 2 = 120$.

questions.stem_md: A collection of frogs has 36 males. Each male has one copulatory pad on each forelimb. How many copulatory pads do the males have in all?
A frog flicks out its tongue and catches a passing moth. Which statement about its tongue is correct?

options.text_md: It is a single lobe fixed at the back of the mouth.
It is bilobed and fixed all round the floor of the mouth.
It is bilobed and fixed at the front of the mouth, with the free ends behind.
It is bilobed and fixed at the back, with the free ends in front.

questions.solution_md: The tongue is attached at the front and its forked free end can be flicked out — option (c).

questions.stem_md: After the stomach, the food of a frog passes into the
questions.solution_md: Chyme passes from the stomach to the duodenum, the first part of the intestine — option (a).

questions.stem_md: The liver of a frog is damaged by a disease. Which secretion would be lacking in the duodenum?
questions.solution_md: The liver makes bile, which is stored in the gall bladder and poured into the duodenum — option (b).

questions.stem_md: The intestine of a tadpole, which eats plants, is many times longer in relation to its body than that of an adult frog. The adult frog has a short alimentary canal because it

options.text_md: eats insects and other animal food

questions.solution_md: A carnivore needs a shorter gut than a plant eater — option (b).

match_right.text_md: Hydrochloric acid and gastric juice digest food

questions.solution_md: Liver makes bile; gall bladder stores it; pancreas makes pancreatic juice; stomach secretes acid and gastric juice.

questions.stem_md: Give a reason: the alimentary canal of a frog is short.

answer.model_answer_md: The frog is a carnivore and its animal food is easy to digest, so a long canal is not needed.

questions.solution_md: Carnivore.

questions.stem_md: Give a reason: a frog that is kept out of water for a long time in a dry place becomes weak.

answer.model_answer_md: Its skin dries, so it cannot exchange gases through the skin.

questions.solution_md: Skin dries.

questions.stem_md: Name the three surfaces through which a frog exchanges gases and state which of them it uses when it is under water.

answer.model_answer_md: A frog exchanges gases through the **skin** (cutaneous respiration), the lining of the **buccal cavity** and the **lungs** (pulmonary respiration). Under water it uses only the **skin**, through which oxygen dissolved in the water diffuses into the blood.

questions.solution_md: Three surfaces; the one used under water.

questions.stem_md: Name the chambers of the heart of a frog and the vessels or structure through which blood enters each atrium.

answer.model_answer_md: The heart has **two atria**, right and left, and **one ventricle**. The **right atrium** receives blood from the body through the **sinus venosus**, into which the veins open. The **left atrium** receives blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.

questions.solution_md: Chambers; entry of blood.

questions.stem_md: Name the two digestive glands of the frog that open into the duodenum and state what each secretes.

answer.model_answer_md: The **liver** secretes **bile**, which is stored in the gall bladder and passes to the duodenum. The **pancreas** secretes **pancreatic juice**, which contains digestive enzymes. Both secretions enter the duodenum through a **common duct** and complete the digestion begun in the stomach.

questions.solution_md: Liver and pancreas.

questions.stem_md: List, in order, the parts of the alimentary canal of a frog, and say what happens to the food in the stomach and in the duodenum.

answer.model_answer_md: The order is **mouth, buccal cavity, pharynx, oesophagus, stomach, duodenum, ileum, rectum and cloaca**. In the **stomach** hydrochloric acid and gastric juice begin the digestion and the food becomes **chyme**. In the **duodenum** the chyme receives **bile and pancreatic juice** through a common duct, and digestion continues.

questions.solution_md: Order; stomach; duodenum.

questions.stem_md: Name the two portal systems of the frog and say what each connects.

answer.model_answer_md: In a **portal system** a vein carries blood from one organ to the capillaries of another before it returns to the heart. The **hepatic portal system** connects the **intestine** to the **liver**. The **renal portal system** connects the **hind limbs and lower body** to the **kidneys**.

questions.solution_md: Two portal systems.

questions.stem_md: A frog is kept in a jar of well-aerated water with wax plugs in its nostrils. It stays alive for many hours. Explain why, and say what changes when it is returned to land.

answer.model_answer_md: Under water the frog uses **cutaneous respiration**: oxygen dissolved in the water diffuses across the **moist skin**, so the plugged nostrils do not matter. When the frog returns to land it breathes in air through the **nostrils**, which fill the **buccal cavity**, and forces the air into the **lungs**, while still exchanging gases through the skin.

questions.solution_md: Skin in water; lungs on land.

marking_scheme.step: Buccal cavity and lungs on land

questions.stem_md: Describe the heart of a frog and state what happens to the blood in the ventricle.

answer.model_answer_md: The heart is enclosed in a **pericardium** and has **three chambers**: right and left **atria** and one **ventricle**. The **sinus venosus** opens into the right atrium, and the **truncus arteriosus** leaves the ventricle. Both atria open into the ventricle, where oxygenated blood from the lungs **mixes** with deoxygenated blood from the body.

questions.solution_md: Chambers; vessels; mixing.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the alimentary canal of a frog, naming at least six parts. [3]
(b) State the part of the canal in which the secretions of the liver and the pancreas are received and name the secretions. [2]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) The **mouth and buccal cavity** with tongue, **pharynx**, **oesophagus**, **stomach**, **duodenum**, **ileum**, **rectum** and **cloaca**, with the **liver**, **gall bladder** and **pancreas** beside the stomach; all labelled.

(b) Both secretions are received in the **duodenum**: the liver gives **bile**, which is stored in the gall bladder, and the pancreas gives **pancreatic juice** with digestive enzymes.

questions.solution_md: Labelled canal; secretions.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the heart of a frog. [2]
(b) Describe how blood reaches the heart from the body and from the lungs, and where it goes next. [2]
(c) Name the two portal systems. [1]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A heart with the **right atrium**, **left atrium**, **ventricle**, **sinus venosus** and **truncus arteriosus**, labelled.

(b) Blood from the **body** enters the **right atrium** through the **sinus venosus**; blood from the **lungs** enters the **left atrium**. Both atria open into the **ventricle**, where the blood mixes, and the ventricle pumps it into the **truncus arteriosus**, which sends it to the lungs, body and head.

(c) The **hepatic portal** and **renal portal** systems.

questions.solution_md: Heart; route of blood; portal systems.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Name the organs of respiration of the frog. [1]
(b) Describe how air gets from the outside into the lungs. [2]
(c) How does the frog breathe when it is buried in mud during hibernation? [2]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) The **skin**, the **buccal cavity** and the **lungs**.

(b) Air enters through the **nostrils** into the **buccal cavity**; when the **floor of the buccal cavity is raised** the air is forced through the **glottis** into the **lungs**, a pair of sac-like organs in the thorax.

(c) During hibernation the frog does not use its lungs; it takes in dissolved oxygen through its **moist skin** from the damp mud and water, and its **metabolic rate is low**, so little oxygen is needed.

questions.solution_md: Organs; path of air; skin in hibernation.

marking_scheme.step: (b) Raised floor forces air into lungs

A frog on land takes up 4 ml of oxygen an hour, 40 percent of it through the skin. How many millilitres does it take up through the lungs and the buccal cavity together?
questions.solution_md: Skin $= 4 \times 40 \div 100 = 1.6$ ml; the rest $= 4 - 1.6 = 2.4$ ml.

questions.stem_md: Describe the path taken by sperms from the testis of a male frog to the outside.

answer.model_answer_md: Sperms leave each **testis** through fine tubes, the **vasa efferentia**, which enter the **kidney**. From the kidney they pass into the **urinogenital duct**, the ureter of the male, which carries them to the **cloaca**, from which they are discharged to the outside.

questions.solution_md: Testis, vasa efferentia, kidney, duct, cloaca.

questions.stem_md: Describe how the ova of a female frog reach the outside after they leave the ovary.

answer.model_answer_md: The ova are released into the **body cavity** and are drawn into the funnels of the **oviducts**. They travel along the **oviducts**, which open **separately** into the **cloaca**, and are laid in water through the cloacal aperture, where they are fertilised outside the body.

questions.solution_md: Body cavity, oviduct, cloaca.

questions.stem_md: Name the three regions of the brain of a frog and give one part of each.

answer.model_answer_md: The **forebrain** includes the **olfactory lobes**, the cerebral hemispheres and the diencephalon. The **midbrain** has a pair of **optic lobes**. The **hindbrain** has the **cerebellum** and the **medulla oblongata**, which continues as the spinal cord.

questions.solution_md: Three regions with parts.

questions.stem_md: Describe the kidneys and the ducts of the urinogenital system of a male frog.

answer.model_answer_md: A pair of dark red, bean-shaped **kidneys** lies on either side of the backbone, each made of many **nephrons**. A pair of yellowish **testes** is attached to the upper part of the kidneys by a fold of peritoneum. From each kidney a **urinogenital duct** carries both urine and sperms to the **cloaca**, and the **urinary bladder** in front of the rectum also opens into the cloaca.

questions.solution_md: Kidneys; testes; ducts.

questions.stem_md: Describe the central nervous system of a frog.

answer.model_answer_md: The **central nervous system** has the **brain** and the **spinal cord**. The brain lies in the **cranium** and has a **forebrain** with olfactory lobes, cerebral hemispheres and diencephalon, a **midbrain** with two optic lobes, and a **hindbrain** with the cerebellum and the medulla oblongata. The medulla oblongata passes out through the **foramen magnum** and continues as the spinal cord.

questions.solution_md: Brain regions; spinal cord.

questions.stem_md: A student dissects a female frog. Name the parts of the reproductive system she should find and say how they differ from the reproductive system of a male in their connection with the kidneys and the cloaca.

answer.model_answer_md: She should find a pair of **ovaries** with many ova, and a pair of coiled **oviducts**. The ovaries have **no functional connection with the kidneys**, whereas the testes of a male are attached to the kidneys. The oviducts open **separately** into the cloaca, apart from the ureters, whereas in the male a single **urinogenital duct** carries both sperms and urine.

questions.solution_md: Parts; two differences.

questions.stem_md: Describe fertilisation and development in the frog.

answer.model_answer_md: During mating the female lays her **ova** in water and the male sheds **sperms** over them, so **fertilisation is external**. A very large number of ova are laid, as many are lost. The fertilised egg develops into a **tadpole**, which changes into an adult by **metamorphosis**; this is **indirect development**.

questions.solution_md: External fertilisation; tadpole.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the urinogenital system of a male frog, naming at least six parts. [3]
(b) What is the use of the cloaca? [1]
(c) Name the nitrogenous waste of the frog. [1]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A pair of **kidneys**, with a **testis** attached to the upper part of each, **vasa efferentia** entering the kidney, a **urinogenital duct** from each kidney to the **cloaca**, and the **urinary bladder** opening into the cloaca; all labelled.

(b) The **cloaca** is the common chamber through which **faeces, urine and sperms** pass to the outside.

(c) **Urea**; the frog is ureotelic.

questions.solution_md: Labelled system; cloaca; urea.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the urinogenital system of a female frog. [3]
(b) State two differences from the male system. [2]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) A pair of **kidneys**, a pair of large **ovaries** with ova, coiled **oviducts**, **ureters** from the kidneys, the **urinary bladder** and the **cloaca**; labelled.

(b) The ovaries have **no connection with the kidneys**, but the testes of the male are attached to the kidneys. In the female the **ureters and oviducts open separately** into the cloaca, while in the male the **urinogenital duct** carries urine and sperms.

questions.solution_md: Labelled female system; two differences.

questions.stem_md:
(a) Draw a labelled diagram of the brain of a frog in dorsal view, naming at least six parts. [3]
(b) Name the part concerned with balance and the part concerned with the sense of smell. [2]

answer.model_answer_md:
(a) Two **olfactory lobes**, two **cerebral hemispheres**, the **diencephalon**, two **optic lobes**, the **cerebellum** and the **medulla oblongata** continuing as the **spinal cord**; the forebrain, midbrain and hindbrain are indicated.

(b) The **cerebellum** is concerned with **balance and muscular coordination**; the **olfactory lobes** are concerned with the sense of **smell**.

questions.solution_md: Labelled brain; balance and smell.
